props.description: The slab door back to the crypt, standing open.
An open doorway at the head of the gallery. Nothing bars it.
A fluted pillar, first of a line of four. Something has been chiselled off it at shoulder height, thoroughly, leaving a pale scar.
Its partner across the aisle, scarred in the same place and the same way.
The third pillar. This one still carries its carving: a procession of small robed figures, all walking south.
The fourth. Its figures walk south too, and the last of them has no head.
A cold brazier at the head of the gallery, choked with grey ash. Whatever burned here burned out a long time before the green fires downstairs were lit.
A cone of fallen ceiling, tiles and mortar, with the dust long settled into it.

props.revealHint: The cold brazier at the head of the gallery is choked with ash, and the nearer pillars are scarred where something was chiselled away at shoulder height. Searching the brazier or those pillars would find it.
props.description: A niche behind a facing stone, at knee height. It holds a stack of six clay tokens, each stamped with the same procession as the far pillars.

dmNotes.overview: A processional gallery, long and narrow, running north from the crypt stair. Four pillars line the aisle. An open doorway at the far end continues north.
dmNotes.sensory: Dry where the crypt was damp, and much colder. Dust hangs in the air where the ceiling has come down. Footsteps carry the whole length and come back.
